title: Agency OS
description: Multi-agent orchestration platform that runs the software lifecycle with specialised AI agents
longDescription: A two-part system: a TypeScript core that owns agent lifecycle, tool execution and persistence, and a Next.js 15 control tower for watching it work. Specialised agents (PM, Architect, Dev, QA, UI) collaborate in a shared workspace through pipelines that move a project from discovery to deployment. Designed MCP-ready so agent capabilities extend without touching the core.

data.label: Web Dashboard
data.description: The control tower — real-time agent monitoring
data.details: Next.js 15 interface for watching agent execution live, inspecting produced artifacts and screenshots, managing user stories and tasks, and monitoring deployments. It observes the core; it does not drive it.

data.label: Agency Core
data.description: Agent lifecycle, state and pipeline execution
data.details: The brain. Owns which agent runs when, how state transitions between discovery, planning and execution phases, and how partial failures are retried. Written in TypeScript/Node so agents and tools share one type system.

data.label: Specialised Agents
data.details: Each agent has a narrow role and a distinct prompt contract, working over a shared workspace. Narrow roles are the point: a single generalist agent degrades on long pipelines, whereas a QA agent that only reviews stays reliable.

data.label: Tool Layer
data.details: The only way an agent touches the world. Centralising execution here is what makes agent actions auditable and constrainable, instead of scattering shell calls through prompt logic.

data.label: LLM Provider
data.details: Accessed behind an adapter so the model choice is a configuration concern, not an architectural one.

data.label: Prisma / Database
data.details: Prisma 7 schema persisting project state, pipeline runs and agent logs. Durable run history is what makes a failed pipeline debuggable after the fact rather than only while it is running.

keyFeatures.title: Narrow agents beat one generalist
keyFeatures.description: PM, Architect, Dev, QA and UI agents each own a role and a prompt contract over a shared workspace. A single generalist degrades on long pipelines; a QA agent that only reviews stays reliable.

keyFeatures.title: One centralised tool layer
keyFeatures.description: Filesystem, Git and test execution live in a single layer instead of scattered through prompt logic, which is what makes agent actions auditable and constrainable.

keyFeatures.title: Durable run history
keyFeatures.description: Prisma persists projects, pipeline runs and agent logs, so a failed pipeline is debuggable after the fact and not only while it is running.

keyFeatures.title: MCP-ready by design
keyFeatures.description: Agent capabilities extend through the Model Context Protocol without changes to the orchestration core.
